clips.text: This night went about as poorly as it could have for Jaylen Brown. They felt like the more well-coached team, the more well-prepared team. They knew what Philly was going to try to throw at them, but Jaylen Brown's mode of attack would be they crowded him, they crowded his line of sight. They knew that he would be trying to get downhill and that he would be looking to score on those drives, and they kept throwing extra bodies at him, arms, length at him. He had several turnovers, then he is getting offensive fouls, then he is fouling guys in the back. He was just off of his game.

The requirements of this offense speak directly to his actual strong suits and skill set. And so you see something seamless happening there, whereas in Philly, it is they have way more to figure out and I thought this game was indicative of that truth. 100% agree. I think you have a team that knows its identity and a team that is still figuring it out. And that to me was the big takeaway on both sides. clips.speaker: Alvan Adams
clips.text: We started last night. We had a great team dinner. Six of us were there and Curtis Perry started us off with a toast to the seven who are gone. The four players, Phil Lumpkin, Nate Hawthorne, Paul Westphal, Dick Van Arsdale, the two coaches, John MacLeod and Al Bianchi, and of course the voice of the Suns, Al McCoy. We were there three hours, 6 to 9 o'clock. We had wives and daughters and grandsons, and we talked about everything from Ricky Sobers, the Enforcer, in all three rounds of the playoffs, to Richie Powers not calling a timeout on Paul Silas in Boston.
clips.news_angle: Alvan Adams on the Suns' team dinner and celebrating the 1976 team

clips.pull_quote: Curtis Perry started us off with a toast to the seven who are gone.

clips.speaker: Alvan Adams
clips.text: I came in as a rookie, as did Ricky Sobers, but listening to John Wetzel and Gar Heard and Curtis Perry talk about it, they were on one or two or three other teams before they came here and they go, there was nothing like the camaraderie and the togetherness and the trust that we had at the end of that season.
clips.news_angle: Alvan Adams on the camaraderie and trust of the 1976 Suns team
clips.social_post: Alvan Adams on the unique chemistry of the 1976 Suns: there was nothing like the camaraderie and the togetherness and the trust that we had at the end of that season.

clips.pull_quote: There was nothing like the camaraderie and the togetherness and the trust that we had.

clips.speaker: Alvan Adams
clips.text: It was one great play after another. It wasn't missed shots. It wasn't turnovers. It was how Alvan Adams doing this, Westphal doing that, Gar Heard hitting that shot. And I had the best seat too, because I fouled out right at the end of regulation. I had the seat right there on the bench, got to see the whole thing.
clips.news_angle: Alvan Adams on why Game 5 of the 1976 Finals remains the greatest game
clips.social_post: Alvan Adams calls Game 5 of the 1976 Finals the greatest game he ever saw, noting he had the best seat in the house on the bench after fouling out.

clips.pull_quote: It was one great play after another. It wasn't missed shots. It wasn't turnovers.

clips.speaker: Alvan Adams
clips.text: I consider it luck and I worked at it too, but I got to work here for 50 years. I worked here from 75 to 2025 in one capacity or another. And so I got to see, I didn't see the first six or seven years that the Suns existed. I know they made the playoffs once against the mighty Lakers, I think it went to seven games. I didn't see any of that, but we came to this team by the time the playoffs hit in 76.
clips.news_angle: Alvan Adams on his 50-year tenure with the Phoenix Suns organization
clips.social_post: Alvan Adams reflects on his incredible 50 year tenure with the Phoenix Suns organization from 1975 to 2025.
clips.video_title: Alvan Adams Media Availability | Phoenix Suns | 11-10-26
clips.pull_quote: I worked here from 75 to 2025 in one capacity or another.

clips.speaker: Alvan Adams
clips.text: They were the defending champions. They had won 59 games, we won 42, were 17 games behind them. So we came in third, I think we were a game behind Seattle. We beat Seattle first. And as I was reading these articles the last couple days, I was reading Bill Russell, the Sonics head coach's comments. He goes, after we won games, I think two, five and six, we beat them in six, he goes, they're just better than us. They're playing better than us. That's what Al Attles of the Warriors said after we beat them. He goes, they're just playing better than us.
clips.news_angle: Alvan Adams on the 1976 Suns playing the defending champion Warriors
clips.social_post: Alvan Adams recalls the 1976 playoff run, sharing how opposing coaches Bill Russell and Al Attles admitted the Suns were simply playing better basketball.
clips.video_title: Alvan Adams Media Availability | Phoenix Suns | 11-10-26
clips.pull_quote: They were the defending champions. They had won 59 games, we won 42, were 17 games behind them.

clips.speaker: Alvan Adams
clips.text: One of my jobs was to be the purchasing agent for all FF&E, all furnishings, fixtures and equipment. One of the things I investigated real closely were basketball standards. There was a company out of Oregon and they had a new goal that they were selling in Europe and the Blazers used at their training camp. In the old days, the support, because I was watching some old video of Dick Van Arsdale getting smashed by Wilton Chamberlain into the old support of just some metal poles crisscrossed and it's only four feet beyond the end the baseline. These new units sat about two feet further back. So I figured it was a safer distance. But I was worried about the longer lever arm. So when Will goes up and dunks it or Mark West goes up and dunks it, how long does it do that before it restores to its quiet position? I decided to go ahead and buy those.
clips.news_angle: Alvan Adams on selecting new basketball standards for the arena
clips.social_post: Alvan Adams shares the technical story behind choosing new basketball standards for the arena to improve player safety.
clips.video_title: Alvan Adams Media Availability | Phoenix Suns | 11-10-26
clips.pull_quote: These new units sat about two feet further back. So I figured it was a safer distance.

clips.speaker: Alvan Adams
clips.text: Our first nationally televised game in this building, us playing Orlando and this new big Shaquille O'Neal, and he didn't even swing on or do a chin up. It was late in the second quarter, he grabbed it and let go and the whole thing quietly went back to its restored position. The NBA people were here, the commissioner was here, the guy I called about the goals, I saw him at halftime. He looked at me and he goes, Alvan, I said, I'm fired. I'm fired. Luckily, at the time the league only required you have a spare backboard because of Darryl Dawkins and those guys used to shout about. We had luckily the old two units from the Coliseum. So we were able to get them out, wipe them down with some paper towels and get it out there and finish the game.
clips.news_angle: Shaquille O'Neal breaks the basketball goal during a televised game
clips.social_post: Alvan Adams recalls the moment Shaquille O'Neal broke the goal in the first nationally televised game at the arena: I looked at the supplier and said I am fired.
clips.video_title: Alvan Adams Media Availability | Phoenix Suns | 11-10-26
clips.pull_quote: Our first nationally televised game in this building, us playing Orlando and this new big Shaquille O'Neal.

clips.speaker: Gilbert Arenas
clips.text: Your shin was hurting in Orlando too? Your shin was aching you in Orlando? Because I've seen the few games you got busy in Orlando. No, it was more so much stuff was happening. Just got off the gun thing. You see me in Chicago, right? So what happened is I'm neutralizing in Orlando. So when I get back to DC, I'm on demon time. Grew the hair. John Wall, check that stuff up. He getting mopped.

clips.speaker: Gilbert Arenas
clips.text: That number one pick, I mean, I mopped him. I watched film on him. I'm like, he's a right-handed that want to go left. So he jump off his right foot, and two-foot jumps off his left with the lean, so he don't have the same power as a righty. I'm like, I'm going to just push him towards his right. People going to think I'm stupid. So I already got this guy down. Meet this guy for the first time, I said, 'Oh, Gil, what's up, OG?' I threw your whole shit off, man. I'm a big fan, dog. I can't wait to play with you, OG.
clips.news_angle: Gilbert Arenas explains his tactical approach to playing against John Wall

clips.pull_quote: He's a right-handed that want to go left. So he jump off his right foot.

clips.speaker: Gilbert Arenas
clips.text: I'm on demon time, man. I'm mad at the whole situation, mad at the organization, man. I'm making everybody pay. And then the dude that's replacing me is like, 'Man, the NBA, man, what's up, man?' I'm like, this is you, dog. This is you. Whatever you need, boss hog, I'm good, man. You don't have to worry about like, I'm adapting to you. How you play the game, where you want me at, that's where it's at, man. This ain't my shit, this is you. It's all you. I'm not even going to be in your way, big dog. And that's how I went into it. But when I got to Orlando, it was more like, it ain't my place. Like this the white place. Like I can't come in and, 'Hey man, hey coach, man, get the fuck out my way, man. What's up?' Like so every time he was forced to play me, like so like J. Rich is out, J.J. Redick out, I'm not, it's just me and Duhan, and he got to play us. Like see, popping my shit.
clips.news_angle: Gilbert Arenas on his frustration with the Washington Wizards organization
clips.social_post: Gilbert Arenas opens up about his frustration with the Wizards organization and his mindset during his transition to the Orlando Magic.
clips.video_title: Gilbert Arenas says he REALLY wanted the SMOKE with John Wall
clips.pull_quote: I'm on demon time, man. I'm mad at the whole situation, mad at the organization.

clips.speaker: Gilbert Arenas
clips.text: Jameer Nelson was this guy. That man Jameer sacrificed. He done went through the mud with you, everything. You can't just say and just come in, I'm going to just play. No. I even told Jameer, like you know how you see like that that unsettling like, 'Ah man, like this kind of shit looking a little stressful out there in the shot,' like, 'Hey, hey, hey, bro. I'm coming off the bench, man. I work the second unit. This is your team.' Because if we got him as the leading point guard, like thinking about like getting yanked out the lineup because the papers writing it, like no, like our unit, you got that unit, J. Rich and them, is me, J.J. Redick, Ryan Nelson, like we good over here. Don't worry about it. I'm not coming for your position. I'm cool with where I'm at.
clips.news_angle: Gilbert Arenas on Jameer Nelson's role in Orlando

Nigga, this is a server. I'm thinking I'm about to sign some autograph. I've been served. You like, what the fuck? Nigga, stop the game. clips.speaker: Draymond Green
clips.text: The win that I'll point the most to throughout this eight-game streak is the Lakers. I think it was really big for us to get that win. Obviously, it was an NBA Cup game, which is always a little more exciting. But even aside from it being an NBA Cup game, that's a team that we played the first game of the season, and we did not look very good. So to come back and play them in game six of the season, after we've kind of gotten our foot in a little bit, that's the win I would point at the most because we were down big in that game. We were down 40 to 15, 25 points at the top of the second quarter, and by halftime, we were tied up 53 to 53. So I would say that right there was the point where we dug in, we started getting stops on the defensive end, and to outscore a team, especially a great offensive team like the Lakers, 40 to 13 for the rest of the second quarter says a lot.
clips.news_angle: Draymond Green on the significance of the Lakers win
clips.social_post: Draymond Green points to the Warriors comeback win against the Lakers as the turning point for the team identity this season. He says the ability to dig in and get stops after being down big was the moment they started to build their identity.
clips.video_title: Draymond Green on Warriors 8-Game Win Streak, Jordan Poole's Return Comments & Doc Rivers vs Giannis
clips.pull_quote: The win that I'll point the most to throughout this eight-game streak is the Lakers.

clips.speaker: Draymond Green
clips.text: I still don't think 11 games into the season you're like, 'Oh man, we have our identity.' You're still growing that, but I would say that is the first game where it's like, 'Yo, we really started to build an identity,' including being down and having the ability to come back. I think three of the next four games we were down 15-plus points and came back and won those games. So, the team started to build an identity in that game, and I think it's been full steam ahead for us since.
clips.news_angle: Draymond Green on the Warriors building their identity
clips.social_post: Draymond Green says the Warriors are still growing their identity 11 games into the season but notes that their ability to overcome double-digit deficits in recent games has been a key step forward for the team.
clips.video_title: Draymond Green on Warriors 8-Game Win Streak, Jordan Poole's Return Comments & Doc Rivers vs Giannis
clips.pull_quote: I still don't think 11 games into the season you're like, 'Oh man, we have our identity.'

clips.speaker: Draymond Green
clips.text: Around the league, when you get a slew of injuries like we've got in the NBA over the past few weeks, teams are able to gain confidence because you look up and you're like, 'Man, it's wide open.' And when that happens, it's just a different mental switch that flips. So, the last three weeks has been great to the Dubs, and we've got to keep it going.
clips.news_angle: Draymond Green on how injuries affect team confidence
clips.social_post: Draymond Green notes that the recent wave of injuries across the NBA has shifted the mental approach for many teams, creating a sense that the league is wide open and boosting confidence for teams like the Warriors.
clips.video_title: Draymond Green on Warriors 8-Game Win Streak, Jordan Poole's Return Comments & Doc Rivers vs Giannis
clips.pull_quote: When you get a slew of injuries like we've got in the NBA over the past few weeks, teams are able to gain confidence.

clips.speaker: Draymond Green
clips.text: Fred VanVleet is the quarterback of that team. He is the floor general that team, and he is the head of the snake. And when he went down last year, that Houston team was never the same. And they were never going to be the same. You take the quarterback off of an NFL team, and they're never the same. And so Fred being back, fully healthy, and it's showing in Houston's game. Marcus Smart has been a big addition for this Houston Rockets team. They're playing really good basketball.
clips.news_angle: Draymond Green on Fred VanVleet's impact on the Rockets
clips.social_post: Draymond Green calls Fred VanVleet the head of the snake for the Rockets and compares his importance to a quarterback in the NFL. He also credits Marcus Smart as a major addition to the Houston rotation.
clips.video_title: Draymond Green on Warriors 8-Game Win Streak, Jordan Poole's Return Comments & Doc Rivers vs Giannis
clips.pull_quote: Fred VanVleet is the quarterback of that team. He is the floor general that team.

clips.speaker: Draymond Green
clips.text: I saw Yaxel had compared the Dubs to the Bad Boys Pistons and I would warn Yaxel he should go watch those Bad Boys Pistons. I don't think we're quite close to who those Bad Boys Pistons were. But, you know, I think any team that's going to have any shot at being a good team has to have an edge. And I think last year we didn't have much of an edge at all. We were a pretty shit team. This year, I think we have a lot more of an edge than we've had. And by the way, don't think that that does not aid in winning. That definitely aids in winning.
clips.news_angle: Draymond Green on Yaxel's 'Bad Boys' comparison
clips.social_post: Draymond Green pushes back on comparisons between the current Warriors and the Bad Boys Pistons, but admits that having an edge is vital to winning and believes this year's team has more of that edge than last year.
clips.video_title: Draymond Green on Warriors 8-Game Win Streak, Jordan Poole's Return Comments & Doc Rivers vs Giannis
clips.pull_quote: I saw Yaxel had compared the Dubs to the Bad Boys Pistons and I would warn Yaxel.

clips.speaker: Draymond Green
clips.text: I love the edge that Georges, you know, has not only brought to our second unit, but that he's brought to the team. Just that fierce competitiveness that he's brought to the team, never backing down, meeting force with force, getting in a few mix-ups. I've always told y'all things like that can jolt a team. And Georges, the role that he's been playing, not being afraid to mix it up, but also the way he's shooting the basketball, scoring the basketball in different ways, he's been a big, big addition. In the press conference the other night, I compared it to Otto Porter and the reality is I compared it to Otto Porter and to Nemanja Bjelica. Those two guys in 2022 were so vital to the team that we became, and neither one of those guys were signed as where people were riding home like, 'Man, the Warriors added those guys, they're going to make a difference in a championship.' Neither one of those guys, anyone said that about. Yet, I can sit here and tell you for certain, those two guys made so much of a difference in us winning a championship in 2022.
clips.news_angle: Draymond Green on Georges Niang's competitive edge
clips.social_post: Draymond Green praises Georges Niang for bringing a fierce competitive edge to the Warriors second unit, comparing his impact to the vital roles played by Otto Porter and Nemanja Bjelica during the 2022 championship run.
clips.video_title: Draymond Green on Warriors 8-Game Win Streak, Jordan Poole's Return Comments & Doc Rivers vs Giannis
clips.pull_quote: I love the edge that Georges, you know, has not only brought to our second unit.

clips.speaker: Draymond Green
clips.text: I was asked some questions last night about Jordan Poole's post-game comments where he spoke about returning to the Dubs and said this place feels like home. And I understand that. Team he was drafted to, the team he's had the most success with, has not quite had a good go at it since leaving here. I completely understand that. I saw on Instagram my clip was, 'I have no issue with that.' I love how all the clickbait media publications try to clip one little piece of what you say and then try to use it to stir up controversy. And all the dummies that then read that one little clip of what you're saying and have this huge reaction, and a lot of the dummies' reactions be, 'You're so dumb and you're an idiot.' And it always baffles me when I sit and read the dummy say, 'You're a dummy, you're an idiot,' when they're clearly dumb because they read five sentences of a two-paragraph excerpt and said, 'You're stupid.' And I can't help for the life of me understand how they don't understand how stupid they are.
clips.news_angle: Draymond Green on Jordan Poole's comments about returning to the Warriors
clips.social_post: Draymond Green calls out clickbait media for trying to stir up controversy over Jordan Poole's recent comments about the Warriors, saying he has no issue with Poole calling his former home a place that feels like home.
clips.video_title: Draymond Green on Warriors 8-Game Win Streak, Jordan Poole's Return Comments & Doc Rivers vs Giannis
clips.pull_quote: I was asked some questions last night about Jordan Poole's post-game comments where he spoke about returning.

clips.speaker: Draymond Green
clips.text: I don't make decisions here. I'm a basketball player. I don't decide my own future here, let alone someone else's. That's the number one. Number two, what I said was also, I'm an adult. So if you're asking me as if that's going to be a problem for me, that's no problem for me. Number one, I'm not someone who walks around with a grudge, and to be honest with you, why would I even walk around with a grudge? That's not really even for me. And so, and that that's what I shared. You know, I like that that don't matter to me. Like that that don't affect me one way or another. I'm not someone that walks around with a grudge. I'm an adult. He's an adult. We will figure it out how adults figure it out. And man, it's become a relationship that I actually cherish. I cherish my relationship with CP. But my point when, and I told Mike then, I said, 'Mike, listen, me and Chris Paul have not seen eye to eye. It's my brother now, but we've not seen eye to eye in our career.' Can't say that I'm very fond of him at all. What I can tell you is that will not be an issue. I'm an adult, he's an adult. We will figure it out how adults figure it out.
clips.news_angle: Draymond Green on his relationship with Jordan Poole
clips.social_post: Draymond Green on his relationship with former teammates: I am an adult, he is an adult, we will figure it out. I do not walk around with a grudge.
clips.video_title: Draymond Green on Warriors 8-Game Win Streak, Jordan Poole's Return Comments & Doc Rivers vs Giannis
clips.pull_quote: I don't make decisions here. I'm a basketball player. I don't decide my own future here.

clips.speaker: Draymond Green
clips.text: Jimmy Butler worked out in his full Warriors uniform on Saturday. Jimmy Butler also worked out in his full Warriors uniform on Monday. It's crazy because this isn't the first time I've seen like guys get in their full game uniform and workout. When Klay was rehabbing from his ACL or was it the Achilles? The Achilles, I want to say. Either the one, he would be in there in his full uniform during his workout. And I don't know what it is. I'm grateful that I haven't had to experience that, but I think, you know, it just kind of gives those guys like, rehab can be very tedious, and I have been through a lengthy rehab, not the length of that, but I have been through a lengthy rehab and it gets very tedious, mundane, same thing over and over and over again. And I think for those guys, they just want to feel the game. They want to feel the uniform, they want to feel a little different than what they felt throughout this entire rehab process. Jimmy's been on this rehab journey now since February. It's November. Right? So, I think guys kind of get that sense and want to feel that uniform again and wants to feel like, you know, things are getting closer to getting real again.
clips.news_angle: Draymond Green on Jimmy Butler working out in uniform
clips.social_post: Draymond Green discusses why players like Jimmy Butler and Klay Thompson wear full uniforms during rehab workouts, noting that it helps them feel the game and stay connected during the tedious recovery process.

clips.pull_quote: Jimmy Butler worked out in his full Warriors uniform on Saturday. Jimmy Butler also worked out.

clips.speaker: Draymond Green
clips.text: I would never make that bet. Because if we lose and I put on that Wolverine stuff, my skin would melt. Like, you literally see me just sit here and wither on away, just melt right away. I can't put that on. That's like acid, pouring acid on my skin. Putting a scum bum Wolverine shirt, hoodie, jersey, yuck. Yuck. Why would I do that? So, no, I'm not making that bet because when you make a bet, there's a 50/50 chance that you're going to lose. And that's too high of a percentage for me to possibly have to put on some scum bum gear.

clips.social_post: Draymond Green says he would never bet on the Michigan Wolverines because wearing their gear would be like pouring acid on his skin. He refuses to put on any scum bum gear.

clips.pull_quote: If we lose and I put on that Wolverine stuff, my skin would melt.

clips.speaker: Draymond Green
clips.text: When Doc says this, it's similar to Mark Jackson saying that, except when you start saying he doesn't have a super high IQ and he doesn't understand execution, those then come off and allow people to take them as personal shots. You can make the point that you're trying to make without saying he doesn't have a high IQ, without saying he needs to learn how to execute better. You can still make your point and not make it come off as a direct shot at Giannis. But I'll be honest, I don't think Doc was really taking a shot at him. I think Doc was kind of just sharing his truth and what he saw.
clips.news_angle: Draymond Green on Doc Rivers' comments regarding Giannis Antetokounmpo's basketball IQ
clips.social_post: Draymond Green weighs in on Doc Rivers comments about Giannis Antetokounmpo, saying that while Doc might have been sharing his truth, the remarks about basketball IQ and execution come off as a direct shot.
clips.video_title: Draymond Green on Warriors 8-Game Win Streak, Jordan Poole's Return Comments & Doc Rivers vs Giannis
clips.pull_quote: You can make the point that you're trying to make without saying he doesn't have a high IQ.

clips.speaker: Draymond Green
clips.text: We learned this when Mark Jackson said Steph Curry ruined the game. When he said it, I remember everybody, including us, like, 'Damn, why would he say that?' But the reality is, Mark Jackson has had never been more right about anything in his life when he said that. He wasn't saying he ruined the game in a negative way. He was saying he ruined the game like, 'Now you got people who can't shoot threes casting a bunch of threes' because they see him do it and he makes it look so effortless.
clips.news_angle: Draymond Green compares Doc Rivers' comments to Mark Jackson's Steph Curry remarks
clips.social_post: Draymond Green reflects on Mark Jackson saying Steph Curry ruined the game, noting that while it sounded negative at the time, Jackson was right about how Curry changed the way everyone shoots threes.
clips.video_title: Draymond Green on Warriors 8-Game Win Streak, Jordan Poole's Return Comments & Doc Rivers vs Giannis
clips.pull_quote: Mark Jackson has had never been more right about anything in his life when he said that.

clips.speaker: Draymond Green
clips.text: Be very careful with all the Giannis dialogue. Number one, he is a top 20, top 30 player in NBA history. Whether he got a high IQ, whether he execute well, whether he go too fast and crazy downhill, he top 20. So whatever the hell he doing wrong, cool. Maybe it would have took him from top 20 to eight. But top 20 ain't that bad. The Doc Christy one was crazy to me. Like that's wild. Some things, as a wise man once told me, some things are better left unsaid.
clips.news_angle: Draymond Green defends Giannis Antetokounmpo's status as an all-time great player
clips.social_post: Draymond Green defends Giannis Antetokounmpo as a top 20 player in NBA history, saying that regardless of debates over his IQ or execution, his status as an all-time great is secure.
clips.video_title: Draymond Green on Warriors 8-Game Win Streak, Jordan Poole's Return Comments & Doc Rivers vs Giannis
clips.pull_quote: He is a top 20, top 30 player in NBA history.

clips.speaker: Draymond Green
clips.text: Nikola Jokic predicts that the low post would be completely gone from the NBA within five to ten years. He said the low post defenders are allowed to do much more. They can push, grab, and be more physical than they can when defending on the perimeter. And I think that's why players are no longer willing to play in the low post as much. You get fouled, but it's not called. You keep getting tired after every possession. That's why I think the low post is becoming an endangered part of our game and probably five to ten years, it might not even be there anymore. And I would tell Joker, I agree. I think the low post will continue to become more and more extinct.
clips.news_angle: Nikola Jokic believes the low post will soon become extinct

clips.speaker: Draymond Green
clips.text: When I first came in the league 14 years ago, you had two bigs in the low post getting the ball thrown into them and them trying to get a bucket. Everything has changed. We spoke about Stephen Curry earlier, that's a part of the reasoning it changed. Analytics, how much more a three-point shot is worth than a two-point shot. All of these things. I agree with Joker. Also, I agree with them in if you jump in the middle of the lane off a jump hook and you shoot a jump hook and you land on somebody's foot, they ain't calling the flagrant foul. You shoot a jump shot outside of the three and you land on somebody's foot, they're calling the flagrant foul. It is 1,000% refereed differently in them trenches.
clips.news_angle: NBA officiating is inconsistent between the perimeter and the post
clips.social_post: Draymond Green argues that the NBA is officiated differently in the post compared to the perimeter, noting that landing on a foot in the paint is rarely a flagrant foul while the same play on a jump shot is called.
